rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Kafi reports al-Sadiq explaining that twisting the matter and turning away from what was commanded are deeds God knows; al-Tabataba'i groups this among reports counted as corruption reports.
rows.anchor: في قوله تعالى " وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا " قال " إن تلووا الأمر وتعرضوا عما أمرتم به

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: Some occasion reports recast the verse as commanding the Prophet to convey what was revealed about Ali, and say it was revealed concerning him; they are classified among corruption reports.
rows.anchor: الروايات التي تذكر هذه الآية هكذا " يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل اليك في علي " والآية نازلة في حقه

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: Reports say Banu Tamim called the Prophet from outside his chambers, then insert their name into the verse; this led readers to suppose words had dropped from it.
rows.anchor: فذكرت الآية فيها هكذا { إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات } بنو تميم { أكثرهم لا يعقلون } فظن أن في الآية سقطا

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: Application reports gloss those who did wrong as Muhammad's family, treating Qur'anic application to later cases as evidence of textual corruption when it is not.
rows.anchor: من الأخبار الواردة في جرى القرآن وانطباقه

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: Other application reports interpret obedience to God and the Messenger as allegiance to Ali and the Imams after him, a reading the author says was miscounted among corruption reports.
rows.anchor: وما ورد من قوله { ومن يطع الله ورسوله } في ولاية على والائمة من بعده فقد فاز فوزا عظيما

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: In al-Kafi, al-Rida tells Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi to recite al-Ikhlas as people do, with the added devotional phrase “Thus is my Lord” twice; such additions were mistaken for omitted Qur'an.
rows.anchor: عن عبد العزيز بن المهتدي قال سألت الرضا عليه السلام عن التوحيد فقال كل من قرء قل هو الله أحد وآمن بها فقد عرف التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Variants rendering the Badr companions as weak or few instead of humiliated likely paraphrase the meaning, rather than preserve altered Qur'anic wording.
rows.anchor: اختلاف الروايات في لفظ الآية كالتي وردت في قوله تعالى { ولقد نصركم الله ببدر وأنتم أذلة }

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: One report objects that the believers cannot be called humiliated while God's Messenger was among them, supporting a meaning-based explanation of the variants.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده ما ورد في بعضها من قوله عليه السلام لا يجوز وصفهم بأنهم أذلة وفيهم رسول الله

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: Reports about the stoning verse differ in wording and endings, including whether they mention desire or pleasure and whether the ending says God is Wise or Mighty and Wise; such contradiction can invalidate them.
rows.anchor: وربما لم يكن إلا من التعارض والتنافي بين الروايات القاضي بسقوطها كآية الرجم على ما ورد في روايات الخاصة والعامة

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: Transmissions that append material to the Throne Verse give substantially different endings and additions, including divine names and descriptions absent from other versions.
rows.anchor: وكآية الكرسي على التنزيل التي وردت فيها روايات فهي في بعضها هكذا الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم لا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects hadith scholars' claim that variant corruption reports remain probative because they agree on the basic claim: their discrepancies weaken the evidence and undermine one another.
rows.anchor: اختلاف هذه الروايات في الآيات المنقولة غير ضائر لاتفاقها في أصل التحريف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insertion and fabrication are widespread in transmitted reports, as seen in accounts of creation, prophets, earlier peoples, Qur'anic exegesis, and early Islamic events.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ذكرنا من شيوع الدس والوضع في الروايات فلا يرتاب فيه من راجع الروايات المنقولة في الصنع والإيجاد وقصص الأنبياء والأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is the secure foundation of religious knowledge and the enduring proof of prophethood, so enemies of religion had strong reason to target it.
rows.anchor: وأعظم ما يهم أمره لأعداء الدين ولا يألون جهدا في إطفاء نوره وإخماد ناره وإعفاء أثره هو القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Qur'an's authority is voided, prophethood and religious teachings lose their proof; the claim that only communal consensus remains cannot rescue them without a further basis for consensus.
rows.anchor: وببطلان حجة القرآن تذهب النبوة سدى والمعارف الدينية لغى لا أثر لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plausible, evidence-supported possibility that reports were interpolated defeats their legal and rational authority, even when their chains are sound, since sound chains cannot exclude insertion into source books.
rows.anchor: يدفع حجية هذه الروايات ويفسد اعتبارها فلا يبقى معه لها لا حجية شرعية ولا حجية عقلائية

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: Several Sunni transmission routes report the prayers called al-Khal' and al-Hafd as suras, but their wording does not resemble Qur'anic composition.
rows.anchor: كسورتي الخلع والحفد اللتين رويتا بعدة من طرق أهل السنة فسورة الخلع هي بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم اللهم إنا نستعينك ونستغفرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged surah of al-Wilaya and similar fabrications imitate Qur'anic form but depart from ordinary Arabic and fail to attain the inimitable divine style, which natural taste rejects.
rows.anchor: ما أورده بعض الروايات من سورة الولاية وغيرها أقاويل مختلقة رام واضعها أن يقلد النظم القرآني فخرج الكلام عن الأسلوب العربي المألوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who accepted fabricated suras were driven by intense deference to reports and neglect of testing them against the Qur'an; a simple look would have shown these were not divine speech.
rows.anchor: أكثر المعتنين بهذه السور والآيات المختلقة المجعولة إنما دعاهم إلى ذلك التعبد الشديد بالروايات والإهمال في عرضها على الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports conflict with the Qur'an's definitive collective indication, not merely with the apparent wording of the preservation verse or the verse saying falsehood cannot approach it.
rows.anchor: مجرد مخالفتها لظاهر قوله تعالى { إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون } وقوله { وإنه لكتاب عزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extant Qur'an has a coherent miraculous structure that resolves apparent tensions and fully conveys divine knowledge, with its principles, branches, and parts mutually connected.
rows.anchor: القرآن الذي بأيدينا متشابه الأجزاء في نظمه البديع المعجز كاف في رفع الاختلافات المتراءاة بين آياته وأبعاضه غير ناقص ولا قاصر في إعطاء معارفه الحقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponent's claim that ordinary reality makes alteration impossible is an evident overstatement: reason permits a mismatch between composition and reality unless evidence establishes it, and such evidence was given earlier.
rows.anchor: أن دعوى الامتناع العادي مجازفة بينة نعم يجوز العقل عدم موافقة التأليف في نفسه للواقع إلا أن تقوم قرائن تدل على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali's gathering and presentation of the Qur'an does not prove disagreement about religious fundamentals or rulings; any difference could concern the ordering of suras or verses revealed over time.
rows.anchor: جمعه عليه السلام القرآن وحمله إليهم وعرضه عليهم لا يدل على مخالفة ما جمعه لما جمعوه في شيء من الحقائق الدينية الأصلية أو الفرعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Ali's collection differed in religious substance, he would have argued the point as he did elsewhere; no transmitted argument has him cite an omitted verse about his authority or accuse them of deletion.
rows.anchor: ولو كان كذلك لعارضهم بالاحتجاج ودافع فيه ولم يقنع بمجرد إعراضهم عما جمعه واستغنائهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preserving Muslim unity cannot explain rejecting Ali's collection only after the community had settled on its own codex; the alleged motive would apply after public distribution, not during collection.
rows.anchor: وهل كان ذلك حفظا لوحدة المسلمين وتحرزا عن شق العصا فإنما كان يتصور ذلك بعد استقرار الأمر واجتماع الناس على ما جمع لهم لا حين الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is implausible that thousands of omitted verses all concerned Ali's authority or were hidden from most Muslims, given the community's desire to learn revelation and the Prophet's effort to teach it.
rows.anchor: هل يسعنا أن ندعي أن ذاك الجم الغفير من الآيات التي يرون سقوطها وربما ادعوا أنها تبلغ الألوف كانت جميعا في الولاية أو كانت خفية مستورة

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: Some reports claim over a third of the Qur'an, more than two thousand verses, fell between two passages of al-Nisa; Sunni reports also say al-Tawba once had a basmala and matched al-Baqara, and al-Ahzab was longer than al-Baqara by two hundred lost verses.
rows.anchor: ما يشير إليه بعض المراسيل أنه سقط في آية من أول سورة النساء بين قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal to abrogation of recitation does not resolve the claims: the interpreters distinguish recitation-and-ruling abrogation from recitation-only abrogation, such as the stoning verse, while other supposedly abrogated rulings remain in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: كانت منسوخة التلاوة كما ذكره جمع من المفسرين من أهل السنة حفظا لما ورد في بعض رواياتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If recitation was abrogated because the passages lacked divine qualities, their removal conflicts with the Qur'an's descriptions of itself as preserved, mighty, free of falsehood, decisive, guidance, light, and a criterion.
rows.anchor: فما معنى الآيات الكثيرة التي تصف القرآن بأنه في لوح محفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad, unqualified contexts of these descriptions do not permit restricting protection, decisiveness, guidance, light, and miraculousness to only the verses still recited.
rows.anchor: فهل يسعنا أن نقول إن هذه الآيات على كثرتها وإباء سياقها عن التقييد مقيدة بالبعض فبعض الكتاب فقط وهو غير المنسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making useful speech permanently unrecited and forgotten renders it void and abandoned, which is incompatible with the Qur'an being a reminder.
rows.anchor: وهل جعل الكلام منسوخ التلاوة ونسيا منسيا غير إبطاله وإماتته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i concludes that corruption reports transmitted by both Muslim groups, as well as reports that Qur'anic recitation was abrogated, categorically contradict the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: فالحق أن روايات التحريف المروية من طرق الفريقين وكذا الروايات المروية في نسخ تلاوة بعض الآيات القرآنية مخالفة للكتاب مخالفة قطعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports comparing this Muslim community's events with those of Israel are well established, but the analogy is not in every respect; reason and necessity rule out that reading.
rows.anchor: لكن هذه الروايات لا تدل على المماثلة من جميع الجهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy concerns shared outcomes and effects; it can refer to sectarian division into 73 Muslim sects, compared with 72 Christian and 71 Jewish sects, a report some call recurrently transmitted.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالمماثلة هي المماثلة في الجملة من حيث النتائج والآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community's division can mean distortion of interpretation: rival groups all rely on the same Book but misplace its words, interpret by opinion, or trust exegesis reports without checking them against scripture.
rows.anchor: من جهة تحريف الكلم عن مواضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy reports do not prove textual corruption; the subset that explicitly describes alteration or omission is unsound and contradicts the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: هذه الطائفة على ما بها من السقم مخالفة للكتاب كما تقدم

rows.speaker: اليعقوبي
rows.claim: Yaqubi reports that after heavy Qur'an-reciter deaths at Yamama, Umar pressed Abu Bakr to collect the Qur'an; Abu Bakr initially objected that the Prophet had not done it, then agreed and appointed Quraysh and Ansar to write and consult Sa'id ibn al-As.
rows.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب لأبي بكر يا خليفة رسول الله إن حملة القرآن قد قتل أكثرهم يوم اليمامة فلو جمعت القرآن فإني أخاف عليه أن يذهب حملته

rows.speaker: اليعقوبي
rows.claim: A report says Ali collected the Qur'an after the Prophet's death, brought it on a camel, and had divided it into seven parts.
rows.anchor: أن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام كان جمعه لما قبض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأتى به يحمله على جمل فقال هذا القرآن قد جمعته

rows.speaker: أبو الفداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Fida reports that many reciters died fighting Musaylima, so Abu Bakr gathered the Qur'an from oral recitation, palm stalks, and hides, then kept it with Hafsa.
rows.anchor: أمر بجمع القرآن من أفواه الرجال وجريد النخل والجلود

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: In Bukhari's report, Zayd says Abu Bakr, urged by Umar after Yamama, commissioned him to collect the Qur'an; Zayd gathered it from palm material, stones, and people, found the end of al-Tawba only with Khuzayma, and the sheets passed from Abu Bakr to Umar to Hafsa.
rows.anchor: أخرج البخاري في صحيحه عن زيد بن ثابت قال أرسل إلي أبو بكر مقتل أهل اليمامة فإذا عمر بن الخطاب عنده فقال أبو بكر إن عمر أتاني

rows.speaker: يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Dawud transmits that Umar asked people to bring what they had learned from the Prophet, which they had written on sheets, boards, and palm stalks, and required two witnesses before accepting material.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يكتبون ذلك في الصحف والألواح والعسب

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: An interrupted-chain report from Urwa says Abu Bakr told Umar and Zayd to sit at the mosque entrance and write anything brought with two witnesses.
rows.anchor: أن أبا بكر قال لعمر ولزيد اقعدوا على باب المسجد فمن جاءكما بشاهدين

rows.speaker: الليث بن سعد
rows.claim: Ibn Ashta's report says Zayd required two just witnesses for each verse; the final al-Tawba passage was accepted from Abu Khuzayma because the Prophet counted his testimony as two, while Umar's unsupported stoning verse was not written.
rows.anchor: فكان لا يكتب آية إلا بشاهدي عدل

rows.speaker: يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Dawud reports that al-Harith ibn Khuzayma brought the final two verses of al-Tawba with testimony that he heard them from the Prophet; Umar confirmed it and said three verses would have formed a separate sura, so these were appended to the last sura.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر وأنا أشهد لقد سمعتهما ثم قال لو كانت ثلاث آيات لجعلتها سورة على حدة

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A report from Ubayy says the compilers thought al-Tawba 9:127 was the last revelation, but the Prophet had afterward recited the final two verses of the sura to him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب أنهم جمعوا القرآن فلما انتهوا إلى الآية التي في سورة براءة

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: A report attributed to Zayd says the Prophet died before the Qur'an had been gathered into a single object; al-Tabataba'i interprets reports of collecting during the Prophet's life more narrowly below.
rows.anchor: حدثنا إبراهيم بن يسار حدثنا سفيان بن عيينة عن الزهري عن عبيد عن زيد بن ثابت قال قال قبض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يكن القرآن جمع في شيء

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Al-Hakim transmits Zayd saying they arranged the Qur'an from loose sheets in the Prophet's presence.
rows.anchor: وفي مستدرك الحاكم بإسناده عن زيد بن ثابت قال كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم نؤلف القرآن من الرقاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i takes reports of collection during the Prophet's lifetime to mean joining piecemeal verses to suras or grouping similar suras; a single codex was unquestionably assembled only after his death.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد ضم بعض الآيات النازلة نجوما إلى بعض السور أو إلحاق بعض السور إلى بعضها مما يتماثل صنفا

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Al-Nasa'i reports Ibn Umar saying he had gathered the Qur'an and recited it each night, until the Prophet told him to complete it in a month.
rows.anchor: " عن ابن عمر قال جمعت القرآن فقرأت به كل ليلة فبلغ النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال اقرأه في شهر "

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: A report graded hasan says five Ansar gathered the Qur'an during the Prophet's lifetime: Muadh ibn Jabal, Ubada ibn al-Samit, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu al-Darda, and Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.
rows.anchor: بسند حسن عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال جمع القرآن على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم خمسة من الأنصار معاذ بن جبل وعبادة بن الصامت

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin's report names Muadh, Ubayy, and Abu Zayd as undisputed collectors during the Prophet's life, while the identity of the fourth is disputed among Abu al-Darda, Uthman, and Tamim al-Dari.
rows.anchor: عن ابن سيرين قال جمع القرآن على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أربعة لا يختلف فيهم معاذ بن جبل وأبي بن كعب وأبو زيد

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi's report lists Ubayy, Zayd, Muadh, Abu al-Darda, Sa'id ibn Ubayd, Abu Zayd, and Mujamma ibn Haritha as collectors in the Prophet's time; one had received all but two or three suras.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي قال جمع القرآن في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ستة أبي وزيد ومعاذ وأبو الدرداء وسعيد بن عبيد وأبو زيد ومجمع بن حارثة

rows.speaker: ابن بريدة
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Burayda calls Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, the first to gather the Qur'an in a codex; he vowed not to wear his cloak until he had done so.
rows.anchor: عن ابن بريدة قال أول من جمع القرآن في مصحف سالم مولى أبي حذيفة أقسم لا يرتدي برداء حتى يجمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports just cited show people gathered revealed suras and verses; they do not establish an arrangement matching either today's order or another order. This was the first collection under Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: أقول أقصى ما تدل عليه هذه الروايات مجرد جمعهم ما نزلت من السور والآيات

rows.speaker: اليعقوبي
rows.claim: Yaqubi says Uthman made a second collection amid disagreement and variant readings, grouped long suras together and short ones together, gathered regional codices, then boiled them in water and vinegar or, according to another account, burned them, sparing Ibn Masud's codex.
rows.anchor: وقد جمع القرآن ثانيا في عهد عثمان لما اختلفت المصاحف وكثرت القراءات

rows.speaker: اليعقوبي
rows.claim: In Yaqubi's account, Ibn Masud refused to surrender his codex, Uthman had him dragged and broke two ribs, and Aisha protested; Uthman sent standard codices to provinces and required people to read from one copy.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود بالكوفة فامتنع أن يدفع مصحفه إلى عبد الله بن عامر

rows.speaker: اليعقوبي
rows.claim: Yaqubi gives differing explanations for standardization: Uthman heard people claim rival family codices, while another version says Ibn Masud had requested a single copy and Huzayfa had written to him.
rows.anchor: وكان سبب ذلك أنه بلغه أن الناس يقولون قرآن آل فلان

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Bukhari reports from Anas that Hudhayfa, alarmed by reading disagreements among Syrian and Iraqi troops, urged Uthman to unify the community; Uthman borrowed Hafsa's sheets and appointed Zayd, Ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn al-As, and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith to copy them.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري عن أنس أن حذيفة بن اليمان قدم على عثمان وكان يغازي أهل الشام في فتح أرمينية وأذربيجان مع أهل العراق فأفزع حذيفة اختلافهم في القراءة

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman instructed the three Quraysh scribes to use Quraysh speech if they and Zayd differed, saying the Qur'an had been revealed in their language.
rows.anchor: وقال عثمان للرهط القرشيين الثلاثة إذا اختلفتم أنتم وزيد بن ثابت في شيء من القرآن فاكتبوه بلسان قريش

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: After copying the sheets, Uthman returned them to Hafsa, sent a copy to every region, and ordered other Qur'anic sheets or codices burned.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا نسخوا الصحف في المصاحف رد عثمان الصحف إلى حفصة وأرسل إلى كل أفق بمصحف مما نسخوا وأمر بما سواه من القرآن

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd says that during copying he recalled a verse from al-Ahzab that he had heard the Prophet recite; they found it with Khuzayma ibn Thabit and added it to its sura.
rows.anchor: قال زيد آية من الأحزاب حين نسخنا المصحف قد كنت اسمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ بها فالتمسناها فوجدناها مع خزيمة بن ثابت

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Abu Qilaba's report says disputes among boys and teachers led Uthman to convene the Companions for a master copy; they consulted someone who had heard the Prophet's reading when verses were disputed and left space for the wording.
rows.anchor: عن أبي قلابة قال حدثني رجل من بني عامر يقال له أنس بن مالك قال اختلفوا في القرآن على عهد عثمان حتى اقتتل الغلمان والمعلمون

rows.speaker: كثير بن أفلح
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Dawud reports that Uthman appointed twelve Quraysh and Ansar to copy sheets from Umar's house; they postponed disputed passages, which Muhammad thought might allow them to consult the latest recitation.
rows.anchor: جمع له اثنى عشر رجلا من قريش والأنصار فبعثوا إلى الربعة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In a sound-chain report from Suwayd ibn Ghafla, Ali says Uthman acted with the group's agreement; they endorsed unifying readings in one codex to prevent schism and disagreement.
rows.anchor: بسند صحيح عن سويد بن غفلة قال قال علي لا تقولوا في عثمان إلا خيرا فوالله ما فعل الذي فعل في المصاحف إلا عن ملاء منا

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: A report says Uthman proposed dropping the waw in al-Tawba's phrase about those who hoard gold and silver; Ubayy threatened to take up his sword unless it was retained, so they included it.
rows.anchor: عن علباء بن أحمر أن عثمان بن عفان لما أراد أن يكتب المصاحب

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, Uthman explains that the Prophet directed where newly revealed verses belonged; because al-Anfal and al-Tawba had similar stories and he died before clarifying their relation, Uthman placed them together without a basmala.
rows.anchor: قال قلت لعثمان ما حملكم على أن عمدتم إلى الأنفال وهي من المثاني
